tasks.task: Read the client brief and clarify it
tasks.what: Understand what the personas are for, at which level, and on which scope.
tasks.how:
Decide the persona level: BRAND personas (people engaging with a brand, segmented on their relationship to it) or CATEGORY personas (people expressing a need in a category, segmented on need / pain point and expertise).
List the scope: markets, languages, period, platforms, expected deliverable (overview slide + 1 deep dive per persona, or one comparison table), expert / HCP profile in scope or not.
Check if Semantiweb already worked for THIS client on the same scope (category audit, tribes sourcing): reuse its desk research and queries as a starting point.
tasks.watch_out:
If the brief describes groups sharing a culture, rituals or a cause, the client may want tribes / communities, not personas: clarify before going further.
If the client expects exact age, income or household data, say early that social data gives inferred generations and lifestyle signals only.
tasks.output: Validated business question, persona level, scope

tasks.task: Write the internal brief and open the decision log
tasks.what: Align the team on objective, scope, timeline and roles.
tasks.how:
Internal brief (Google Doc in the Project Drive): objective, persona level, markets, platforms, period, KPIs to observe (step 2.1), timeline, who does what.
Decision log (sheet in the Project Drive): one line per scope decision with date and who decided (e.g. "resellers excluded", "HCP profile shown separately", "CN period extended to 24 months").
Allocate time in Float and plan client touchpoints.
tasks.watch_out: Log every scope call: it is what you will rely on when the client questions a choice.
tasks.output: Internal brief + decision log shared with the team

tasks.what: Understand the brand / category and build a first list of possible personas with the project lead.
tasks.how:
Desk research: brand or category news, key launches, drops, collabs, events, controversies over the period; how consumers talk about it on each platform (scroll Instagram, TikTok, RED, Reddit with the main hashtags).
Market specifics: which platforms matter per market (e.g. CN: RED, Douyin, Weibo), local vocabulary and slang, generational codes.
Hypothesis session with the project lead: list possible personas, each with (1) why they engage, (2) the signals that would reveal them: keywords, hashtags, expressions, content formats (OOTD, haul, review, GRWM), brands they co-cite.
Turn the signals into a keyword list per language: it feeds the main query (1.2) and later the persona queries (2.4).
Done when: hypothesis list with signals is validated by the project lead.
tasks.watch_out:
Hypotheses are a starting point: expect some to disappear, merge or appear during reading.
Have local keywords checked by a native speaker.
tasks.output: Hypothesis list with signals + keyword list per language

tasks.task: Build the main query in Radarly
tasks.what: Capture consumer conversations about the brand / category in scope.
tasks.how:
Build the Boolean query in Radarly from the keyword list: brand or category terms and variants, products, key hashtags, local language terms.
Sources: platforms where consumers talk about themselves (Instagram, TikTok, RED, Douyin, Weibo, Reddit, blogs & forums, YouTube, Pinterest, X, Facebook, depending on markets).
Add exclusions so the corpus stays consumer: brand-owned accounts, official retailers, resellers, media and press, giveaways and contests, bots, fan accounts reposting campaign content.
Check quality on the RANDOM display of posts (not top posts): read posts, spot noise, add exclusions, repeat.
Use the Radarly query skill to reuse validated patterns.
Done when: random reading shows mostly relevant consumer posts and the project lead validates the query.
tasks.watch_out:
Spike from a news or celebrity event: exclude or cap the period and log it in the decision log.
Radarly character / term limits: split into several queries.

tasks.what: Complete Radarly with TikTok content when TikTok matters for the scope.
tasks.how:
Select the brand and consumer hashtags in scope from the desk research.
Send the crawl request as early as possible: crawls can take up to a full day to come back.
Save the crawl output in the Project Drive.
Done when: crawl output is received and readable.
tasks.watch_out: Send the crawl request on day 1 of desk research so it does not block analysis.
tasks.output: TikTok crawl output in Project Drive

tasks.task: Check volumes and depollute, validate with the project lead
tasks.what: Make sure the corpus is clean and volumes are usable per market.
tasks.how:
In Radarly, check volumes per market, platform and month.
Read posts on the random display to depollute; add exclusions to the query if needed.
Note volumes per market: they explain later why a market is more or less represented.
Done when: the project lead validates volumes and depollution.
tasks.watch_out: If a market is mostly media or resellers after cleaning, decide with the project lead whether it is reported as directional only.

tasks.what: Agree what will be described for every persona before reading.
tasks.how:
Core KPIs: motivation / relationship to the brand or category, generation, gender (only when explicit), platforms, centers of interest, behaviors (purchase habits, content formats), brands co-cited.
Optional KPIs depending on the brief: when (timing, occasions), for whom (self / gift), top hashtags, top trends, pain points, solutions used, expertise level, values & expectations, market-specific behaviors.
Create a working sheet in the Project Drive: one tab per persona hypothesis, one line per KPI, plus a "verbatims" zone (text + link + market).
tasks.watch_out: Pick only the KPIs the client will use: they become the blocks of the deep-dive slide.

tasks.what: Get a first view of which hypotheses are supported by the data, and which signals were not expected.
tasks.how:
In the Radarly project, look at facets per market and platform: top words, hashtags, co-cited brands, sources, top authors, clusters.
For each hypothesis, note in the working sheet the facet signals that support it (e.g. "#ootd + several luxury houses co-cited", "drop names peaking on release dates").
Note strong signals that match no hypothesis: they may reveal a missing persona.
Done when: each hypothesis has supporting signals (or none), and unexpected signals are listed.
tasks.watch_out: A hypothesis with no signal in the facets is not dead yet: check it in reading (some behaviors are visual and do not show in words).
tasks.output: Signals per hypothesis in the working sheet

tasks.task: Read posts and check author profiles to confirm the personas
tasks.what: Confirm, adjust, merge or add personas and describe each one.
tasks.how:
For each hypothesis, filter the corpus on its signals (keywords, hashtags) and read posts on the random display, plus the TikTok crawl output.
For representative posts, open the author profile: bio, recent posts, other brands worn or cited, lifestyle, age cues (stated age, school / work, life stage). This is how generation is assessed.
Fill the working sheet as you read: motivation, behaviors, interests, platforms, generation cues, verbatim candidates (exact text + link + market).
Merge two hypotheses when you cannot tell their authors apart by WHY they engage; split one when it groups authors with different motivations; add a persona when unexpected signals hold.
Keep reading until new posts and profiles stop adding new information. There is no fixed number of posts.
Review the persona list with the project lead.
Done when: the project lead validates the final list, each persona with a one-sentence definition ("She / he engages with [brand] because...").
tasks.watch_out:
Do not label a persona from a few very visible creators: check that everyday consumers show the same profile.
Do not infer generation from a photo alone.
tasks.output: Validated persona list, working sheet filled per persona

tasks.what: Give each persona a share of conversations (base 100).
tasks.how:
Build one query per persona on top of the main query, using the signals confirmed in 2.2 and 2.3 (keywords, hashtags, expressions).
Check each persona query on the random display: are the posts really from this persona?
Calculate the share: volume of each persona query / sum of all persona query volumes, so that shares add up to 100. Do it per market if market splits are shown.
Adjust the shares based on the qualitative reading when a query clearly over- or under-captures a persona (e.g. visual behaviors that words do not catch, overlap between two persona queries). Write each adjustment and its reason in the decision log.
Round to whole numbers; totals must equal 100.
Done when: shares are validated by the project lead and adjustments are logged.
tasks.watch_out: Shares are a split of persona conversations, not of consumers: write the base in the slide footnote.

tasks.what: Turn the working sheet into a persona portrait.
tasks.how:
Name (2 to 3 words, consumer-native) + tagline (one line on the core behavior).
"In a nutshell": a short first-person line summarizing the mindset, written by Semantiweb.
Description of 60 to 90 words: how she / he engages with the brand or category, what drives it, how it shows (concrete products, drops, rituals), what role the brand / category plays for them.
3 to 5 centers of interest (topics they care about) and 3 to 5 behavioral insights (what they do).
2 to 3 verbatims picked from the working sheet, kept exactly as posted, with translation if needed.
Optional KPIs agreed in 2.1.
Done when: every attribute can be traced back to posts or profiles read.
tasks.watch_out: If a description could apply to another brand, it is too generic: add the specific behaviors and references you saw.

tasks.how:
One visual per persona showing its behavior and style, consistent style across personas.
Use licensed images, client assets, or AI-generated images if the client allows it.

tasks.what: Lock the structure and headlines before building slides.
tasks.how:
Typical structure: methodology & scope, persona overview slide, one deep dive per persona (or one comparison table for category personas), implications for the client, limitations.
Write the headline of each slide first, as an insight (what it means for the client), then validate the flow with the project lead.
tasks.watch_out: Building slides before the storyline is locked usually means rework.

tasks.what: Produce the overview and deep-dive slides.
tasks.how:
Overview slide: all personas with name, visual, share (%), generation; optional grouping into macro-families; base footnote.
Deep dive per persona: name + tagline, in a nutshell, share (%), generation, platforms, description (4 to 6 key phrases in bold), centers of interest (icons), behavioral insights, verbatims (original + translation), source line "Source: Sample of posts [markets], [period], [platforms]". Same blocks for every persona.
One comparison table can replace deep dives (rows such as age, expertise level, top pain points, solutions used, values & expectations, interests / lifestyle).
tasks.watch_out: Check brand, product and collab names against official sources.

tasks.what: Make the numbers and choices understandable for the client.
tasks.how:
Methodology: markets, period, platforms, tools used (Radarly, TikTok crawls), how personas were identified (hypotheses, facets, reading, author profiles), how shares were calculated (one query per persona, base 100, qualitative adjustment).
Limitations where they apply: social data over-represents vocal and visual users; generations are inferred from profiles; partial coverage of some platforms or markets.
tasks.watch_out: Keep it short: the client should understand what a % means in one read.

tasks.what: Make sure the deck is correct and clean.
tasks.how:
Shares add up to 100 and match the sizing table.
Each verbatim matches the original post (wording, persona, market); translations re-read by a native speaker.
Spelling, brand names, consistent persona names across slides.
Remove annotations, placeholders, internal notes; do not share queries.
Final review with the project lead.
tasks.watch_out: After any last-minute merge or renaming, recheck the shares.

tasks.what: Integrate client feedback before final delivery.
tasks.how:
Present the persona list and shares to the client if timing allows.
Apply feedback and update the decision log.
tasks.watch_out: See barriers table for frequent client requests.

tasks.how:
Assign speakers per persona; prepare one extra real example per persona.
Action feedback and send the final version within the week.
Archive the working sheet, persona queries, sizing table and decision log in the Project Drive for the next wave.
tasks.watch_out: For recurring clients, keep persona definitions stable between waves so they can be compared.
